Web Application Security: Build It Like Someone Will Try to Break It

A beautiful, fast website means little if its security has a giant crack in the door.


Web application security protects websites, users, systems, and sensitive information from attacks and unauthorized access.


Think Security from the start


Before building, ask yourself:


  • What information are we collecting?
  • Who should access it?
  • How are passwords protected?

The CIA Triad


Security focuses on three goals:


  • Confidentiality: Keep information private.

  • Integrity: Keep information accurate and protected.

  • Availability: Keep systems accessible when needed.

Know the Risks


The OWASP Top 10 highlights common web application risks, including broken access control, security misconfiguration, injection, authentication failures, and software or data integrity failures.


A few important habits can make a big difference:


  • Treat user input as untrusted.
  • Use HTTPS.
  • Protect accounts with strong authentication.
  • Keep software and plugins updated
  • Collect only necessary personal information.
  • Check third party services carefully.
